Could you clarify which specific Rules of React are being violated in the
inlined example?

While the LLM explanation provides some general context, it would be
helpful to understand exactly why the compiler treats the inlined version
differently than the version with separate variables, as both appear to
follow standard hook patterns.

On Tue, Jun 30, 2026, 9:49 PM MaxwellCohen ***@***.***> wrote:

> *MaxwellCohen* left a comment (react/react#36847)
> <https://github.com/react/react/issues/36847#issuecomment-4849820001>
>
> The React compiler relies on assumptions about dependencies and pure
> functions to provide memoization; when the assumptions are not met, the
> compiler will bail out. React is compiled to "just JS" at the end of the
> day, and JS allows you to do a lot of dynamic stuff that can be sub-optimal.
>
> The React Compiler doesn't memoize this hook because it violates the Rules
> of React in ways that make automatic memoization unsafe or impossible. You
> can see a full explanation from an LLM <https://t3.chat/share/yl29n7n0xq>
